Consult Summary:
- Telemedicine consult for new-onset left-sided throbbing headache with photophobia x ~1 day; likely migraine; advised NSAIDs with paracetamol, hydration, safety-netting, and BP check.

History:
- Presenting complaint: Severe throbbing headache since waking yesterday; predominantly left-sided; fluctuates in intensity but never fully resolves; photophobia; improved when lying down; worse in bright light/sunlight.
- Associated symptoms: Denies visual changes, abnormal smells/tastes, nausea/vomiting, fever (no thermometer at home), URI symptoms, weakness/tingling/numbness.
- Pertinent negatives: No prior history of regular headaches; not clearly linked to menstrual cycle (last period ~1 week ago); not worse with cough/sneeze; eating and drinking okay.
- Past medical history: No significant medical/surgical history reported.
- Family history: Mother with high blood pressure and migraines.
- Medications: 
  - Microgynon oral contraceptive pill (dose/route/frequency not documented) — started ~6 years ago.
  - Paracetamol for current headache (dose/route/frequency not documented).
- Allergies: Aspirin — causes nausea (“feel really sick”).
- Social history: Lives with housemates; alcohol a few drinks on weekends; non-smoker; denies recreational drug use.
- Preventive care: Blood pressure reportedly normal at last check ~6 months ago.

Examination:
- 

Impression:
- Likely migraine (new-onset unilateral throbbing headache with photophobia, no red-flag symptoms elicited on history).

Plan:
- Analgesia: Start an NSAID (e.g., ibuprofen) together with paracetamol for symptomatic relief (dose/route/frequency not documented). Avoid aspirin due to reported reaction.
- Supportive care: Maintain good hydration; rest in a dark/quiet room.
- Safety-netting: Seek urgent medical attention if headache worsens, changes character, persists without improvement, or if high temperature/fever, rash, or new neurological symptoms develop.
- Follow-up: 
  - Arrange a blood pressure check.
  - Obtain a home thermometer to monitor temperature.
  - If headaches become persistent, recur, are associated with menstrual cycle, or specific triggers emerge, schedule further evaluation.

Quality checks:
● Missing expected elements: In-person vitals (including temperature) and neurological exam; medication doses/routes/frequencies; comprehensive allergy list; pregnancy status not discussed; fundoscopic exam not performed; detailed red-flag screening (e.g., thunderclap onset, neck stiffness) not fully documented.  
● Internal conflicts: None noted.  
● Transcript quality: Minor inaudible/elliptical segments; overall adequate to determine history and plan.
